cross_sdk_exports.scope: Paged execution, continuation source and continuation export suites; every captured file matches byte for byte.

original_instruction_contract: Independent raw bytes and GDT/LDT descriptors in legacy paging and PAE; protected code16/code32, operand16/32, address16/32 and old-SS stack sizing.
All ModRM and SIB memory forms used by this grammar, every segment override, nonflat source caches and source/destination GPR aliasing.
All CPL/RPL/DPL combinations and descriptor types, null loads, descriptor bounds/accessed writes, explicit and implicit-supervisor fault priority, descriptor and operand linear wrap.
A descriptor crossing two pages faults on either read-only page when its accessed bit is clear, including the first page without the accessed bit; an already-accessed descriptor skips that write.

All represented GPRs, valid segment cache fields, visible selectors, unusable bits, operand/descriptor bytes and fault vector/error/CR2, fault-preserved data/same-ring stack caches and the saved outer-ring SS; null-cache hidden fields and exception-delivery writes are explicitly excluded.

Legacy selector operands on both bound core classes use #AC before competing #PF; two-byte alignment for selector MOV/POP/PUSH differs from a four-byte LxS offset field. This does not select the policy of unrelated scalar instructions.

repaired_probe.observation: An initial AfterPaging binding predicted #PF for an original legacy selector MOV that raised #AC. The final test forwards the explicitly selected BeforePaging binding and checks every family on both core classes.

boundaries: This is a transition helper: its caller owns authenticated instruction fetch, EIP/RF completion, persistent interruptibility, event arbitration and fault delivery.
One confined CPU and ordinary RAM; no concurrent descriptor mutation or MMIO.
Unusable null-loaded hidden fields are opaque, and reserved descriptor state outside the loaded-cache contract fails explicitly.
No general legacy/compatibility dispatcher, task/call gates, real/VM86 execution, software SMM, SGX EPC/SSA/AEX or other remaining machine-environment completion is claimed.
Existing native LLVM/NeverC interfaces already transport these instructions. This change adds no compiler builtin, final LLVM release, production SDK pin or gitlink update.
references: Intel SDM revision 093: volume 2 MOV, POP, PUSH and LDS/LES/LFS/LGS/LSS; volume 3A sections 3.4, 6.3-6.6.
